messages:
jess_support: Hey team — customer org `acme-inc` reports that new promo credits (promo_2026_spring) were consumed BEFORE their legacy free-tier credits. They say dashboard showed free credits expiring 2026-08-01 but balance dropped overnight (2026-07-31 PST). Repro steps attached.

olivia_customer: Confirmed. We checked our UI timestamps and logs — balance went from 120 -> 20 around 23:50 PST, we only used ~20 credits. Noticed a promo redemption earlier that day. :thinking_face:

jess_support: Thanks. Our doc says credits burn FIFO by expiry/created_at unless explicit priority set. Can billing/engineering confirm actual runtime ordering?

mike_billing: Looking in the meter. Quick glance: the `credit_allocations` table shows `promo_2026_spring` with `priority=10` for that account. Our billing burn sort order is (priority DESC, expiry ASC, created_at ASC) — so higher priority can indeed be consumed first. Promos should default priority=0. Investigating why this promo has 10.

sara_engineer: Can you paste the redemption/event payload or promo creation record? Any API request IDs?

jess_support: Payload snippet from support logs: ```{"account_id":"org-123","credit_source":"promo_2026_spring","applied_at":"2026-07-31T23:45:12-07:00","priority":10,"amount":100}``` Also saw `redeem_id: rd_9a1b2c`.

mike_billing: Strange. The promo pipeline normally sets priority=0. There's a backfill/migration that ran 2026-07-30 and set `promo_priority` from legacy table — if legacy was NULL we default to 10 (bug).

nick_oncall: FYI deploy-bot shows migration/backfill deployed: `migration/20260730-promo-priority` at 2026-07-30T04:12:00Z. I saw a quick spike in DB writes during that window. Could be the culprit.

sara_engineer: I ran a local repro: create org, add free credits expiring 2026-08-01 amount 100, add promo credits amount 100 created 2026-07-30 with priority 10, then consume 50 via API. Promo credits get consumed first. Repro steps: ```sh
# create free credits (expires 2026-08-01)
POST /v1/admin/credits {"org_id":"org-test","type":"free","amount":100,"expiry":"2026-08-01T00:00:00Z"}
# apply promo (priority=10)
POST /v1/admin/credits {"org_id":"org-test","type":"promo","campaign":"promo_2026_spring","amount":100,"priority":10}
# consume usage
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/usage -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"org_id":"org-test","tokens":50000}'
``` Result: promo decremented first.

mike_billing: Confirmed. For `acme-inc` the migration incorrectly set priority=10 for that promo. Billing will run a recalculation to reassign burned amounts (mark usage as charged against oldest-first) and create a corrective credit/invoice adjustment. ETA ~4 hours.

jess_support: Will we also fix DB defaults to prevent recurrence?

liam_product: We should add a CI test to validate promo priority default and an alert for any promo with non-zero priority unless explicitly specified. Also audit the migration job.

nick_oncall: Rollback plan: run an idempotent patch to set `priority=0` for promos without explicit priority set in source table. Run in staging -> canary -> prod. I'll coordinate.

mike_billing: Customer-facing note: we'll push a `credit_adjustment` line on their next invoice and issue a refund if payment already processed. Dashboard will reflect adjustment after cron job (should appear within 24h, but we'll push event to UI update service ASAP).

olivia_customer: Appreciate the transparency. Please notify when adjustment is posted so we can verify on our end.

jess_support: Will do. Tagging @olivia_customer when done. I'll follow up with a write-up and link to the migration PR and the fix runbook. :thumbsup: 

deploy-bot: migration/20260730-promo-priority deployed by clare_ops at 2026-07-30T04:12:00Z (commit: a1b2c3d).
